Resolve relative paths from the project root

Source: R/utils-project.R
dot-resolve_from_project_root.Rd

Internal helper, the one place the package's path rule is implemented: a relative path is read as relative to the project root, wherever the code happens to be running. NULL stays NULL. Absolute paths (including ~), URLs, NA and empty strings pass through untouched. Everything else is joined to root. The helper is vectorised and keeps the names of path, so a named vector of folders still carries its labels. A value that is not a character vector comes back untouched, for the caller's own validation to reject. .. is not interpreted and ./ is not stripped: use an absolute path to opt out of the rule. The one tidy-up is a bare ".", the default of several arguments, which means the root itself and so becomes root, not root/..

Usage

.resolve_from_project_root(path, root = NULL)

Arguments

path

Character vector or NULL.

root

Character or NULL. The project root. Defaults to .project_root(), which is only evaluated when at least one value needs it.

Value

NULL, or a character vector the same length and with the same names as path.

Details

The helper does not look at the file system and never falls back to anything. Callers that write use it as is. Callers that read use .resolve_input_from_project_root(), which adds the migration fallback.
